subtype: Approach: getting a parent to do the main work [Pitfall]
passage: The school hall smelled of chart paper and glue. Pema's water pump stood on the table, neat and shining, with a typed report beside it. Papa had built it over two evenings and typed the report himself. Ms Disha, the judge, stopped in front of it. "How does the water move up the pipe, Pema?" He glanced at the pump. "Um... Papa put the valve here. I think it goes... in." His ears turned hot. "Which part did you make yourself?" "Colouring the label." She smiled gently, wrote something on her sheet and moved on. Pema stared at the pipe. He could not have explained a single part.

qa.q: Which part of the project did Pema make himself?
qa.a: Pema said he made only the label, by colouring the label.

qa.q: What was Pema feeling when the judge asked how the water moves up the pipe?
qa.a: Embarrassed and a little ashamed, since his ears turned hot and he could not explain his own model.

qa.q: What could Pema and his father do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: Pema could build the parts himself while his father only checks and answers questions, so Pema would understand the pump and could explain it.

qa.q: How might Ms Disha see the model and Pema's answers together?
qa.a: She sees a polished model but a boy who cannot say how it works, which suggests someone else did most of the work, and she responds kindly.

grounding: A boy hands the main work to his father, so the project looks fine but he cannot explain it and learns little.

subtype: Approach: getting a parent to do the main work [Pitfall]
passage: At our school science fair, my table was right next to Jeevan's. His model of a water filter was the best-looking in the hall: clear pipes, three layers of sand and stones, a tap that really dripped. I heard someone say his father had built it over the weekend while Jeevan watched cartoons. The report was typed and printed. When the judge came, she asked, "Why is the charcoal layer in the middle?" Jeevan looked at the model. "Because... it looks nice there?" She asked what the sand did. He said, "Cleans it." "How?" He didn't answer. The judge moved on to me. Jeevan stared at his shoes. I'm not sure what he felt, but he didn't look proud of the beautiful model.

qa.a: It was a model of a water filter.

qa.q: What might Jeevan have been feeling when he stared at his shoes?
qa.a: He was probably embarrassed and a bit ashamed, though the classmate cannot be sure, since he could not explain his own model.

qa.q: Which approach would have suited Jeevan better, and why?
qa.a: Building a simpler model himself with his father's help only where needed, because then he would understand every layer.

qa.q: How might the day look to Jeevan's father?
qa.a: If he hears about the judge's questions, the father might realise that doing the work himself meant Jeevan learned little.

grounding: It shows a child who let his father build the model and write the report, and then could not answer the judge's questions.

subtype: Approach: getting a parent to do the main work [Pitfall]
passage:
Friday: Eshaan's science fair project was a model windmill that lit a bulb. His father, Santosh, was good with tools. "I'll just fix the wires," he said. Eshaan went to play cricket.
Sunday: The windmill was finished, painted and beautiful. The report was typed, with words like "generator" and "current" that Eshaan had never used. He felt pleased and a little strange about it.
Wednesday: At the fair, the judge spun the blades and the bulb glowed. "How does turning make electricity?" Eshaan opened his mouth. Nothing. "What's inside this box?" "Wires," he said quietly. The judge gave a kind smile and wrote something down. On the way home Eshaan said, "Papa, next time, I'll do it and you watch."

qa.q: How did Eshaan feel when he couldn't answer the judge?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and quiet, realising he didn't understand the project that had his name on it.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Eshaan and Santosh work next time?
qa.a: Let Eshaan do each step while Santosh only helps with dangerous tools, so Eshaan learns how it works.

qa.q: How might the fair look to Santosh?
qa.a: Santosh sees the judge's questions go unanswered and hears Eshaan's request, so he may feel sorry he took over.

grounding: It shows a child letting his father build the model and write the report, then being unable to explain it to the judge.
